findings.statement: JAK-STAT pathway activity is raised in inflamed or UC mucosa in all eight cohorts with none decreased; the strongest cohort (GSE193677) has t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=15.68]. This pathway is already drug-targeted (JAK inhibitors), so it is a validated rather than new axis.

CollecTRI STAT3 activity is up in all eight cohorts (GSE193677 t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]), consistent with the JAK-STAT signal. Activity is inferred from target genes, not STAT3 mRNA.

TNFa and NFkB pathway activity are up in all eight cohorts (TNFa in GSE206285 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]). Anti-TNF is already approved, so this confirms an existing target and is not new.

EGFR, Hypoxia, TGFb, MAPK and PI3K are also up in all eight cohorts, and Estrogen, WNT and VEGF in most. Inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so this breadth does not discriminate a target; the specific circuits below are more informative.

Negative result: Androgen pathway activity does not replicate. It is up in some cohorts and down in others, with GSE109142 t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE109142.t=-10.8]. p53 is down in a minority of cohorts and up in none.

CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking (six evidence streams, up in all eight cohorts, meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]). Antagonists (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682) reached phase 2 or phase 3 in other indications, so it is druggable but not yet an approved UC target.

Circuit: neutrophil CXCL8 acts on CXCR2 of neutrophils in the Gubatan single-cell data, e.g. sender Neutrophil CXCR4 to receiver Neutrophil, log2 change vs uninflamed [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755]. This is a feed-forward neutrophil recruitment loop. Co-expression, not proof of signalling.

Neutrophils make most CXCL8 transcripts in inflamed mucosa (share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]), so the ligand of the dominant circuit comes from the same cells that carry its receptor.

Circuit: neutrophil CXCL8 also pairs with ACKR1 on ACKR1 endothelial cells, the highest-scoring CXCL8 pair (Neutrophil CXCR4 to endothelium, score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993]). This suggests an endothelial route for neutrophil entry. ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor, so this is a retention or presentation role rather than classical signalling.

Cell-source caveat: in the Smillie dataset, which has no neutrophils, CXCR2 transcripts sit in T/NK cells at very low rates and do not replicate in the second dataset. In Gubatan, neutrophils make nearly all CXCR2 transcripts (share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]). The tissue signal is therefore infiltrating neutrophils, not an epithelial or stromal change.

Circuit: IL1B from monocyte-derived macrophages and neutrophil states pairs with IL1R2 on neutrophil states (largest gain at the Neutrophil CXCR4 receiver, log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.059]). IL1R2 is a decoy receptor, so this may be a brake as much as a driver. IL-1 is drug-targeted in other diseases (canakinumab) but not in UC.

TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and has nangibotide in phase 2, but the communication tool returned no ligand-receptor pair above the expression thresholds, so no sender-receiver circuit can be assigned in this dataset.

caveats: PROGENy and CollecTRI activities are inferred from target-gene expression in bulk biopsies and mix tissue change with immune infiltration.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression of mean CP10K, not proof of signalling, and come from one single-cell cohort (Gubatan 2026).
Smillie 2019 has no neutrophils, so cell-source shares differ between the two datasets.
The anti-TNF, JAK and IL-23 targets are validated; CXCL8-CXCR2 and TREM1 are not yet UC-approved targets. Neutrophil-directed antagonists carry infection risk, which was not assessed here.
Only a subset of the top-30 convergence candidates was checked for circuits within the tool budget.
